title.en: Making symmetrical designs: rotation and reflection

text.en: Lali draws one small shape and then repeats it by turning and flipping to make a pretty rangoli. Today you become a pattern designer!

To make a firki: take a square paper, fold diagonally both ways, open it to see an X, cut along the four lines halfway to the centre, fold alternate corners to the centre and pin them. It spins and looks the same after every quarter turn.
To make a design with half turn symmetry: draw one shape, then draw the same shape again on the opposite side of the centre, rotated a half turn.
To make a quarter turn design: repeat the shape four times around the centre, each rotated by 1/4 turn.
Check if the design has a line of symmetry: fold it. Some designs have rotational symmetry but no reflection (like a pinwheel with curved blades).
To make a pattern with reflection: draw a vertical line and draw the mirror picture on the other side.
A design looks the same after 1/4 turn only if it can be divided into four identical parts around the centre.
(additional, not in the textbook) Rangoli, kolam and quilt designs use these symmetries.

problem.en: You have a design with one leaf shape. How can you make it look the same after a half turn?

text.en: Draw the same leaf on the opposite side of the centre, rotated half turn.

why.en: Half turn moves a point to the opposite side.

text.en: Now two leaves face opposite ways and the design looks the same after half a turn.

prompt.en: How would you make a design that looks the same after 1/4 turn?

requiredIdeas.en: Each copy is turned a quarter turn about the centre

points.en: Rotational designs repeat a shape around a centre.
1/2 turn symmetry needs 2 identical parts; 1/4 turn needs 4.
Reflection designs repeat a shape as a mirror image.
